subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a static vehicle model using the builder kit's part and extrude/lathe utilities plus a glow effect, deciding I can skip joints since this is a non-articulated model.

Now I'm sketching concrete truck dimensions and layout: a ~7m frame with six wheels on three axles, cylindrical tires with glowing hub rims mounted via mirrored x-offsets, plus fenders and a cab body positioned toward the front with a sloped hood section.

Defining the cab's side profile outline...

Now I'm placing the windshield as a thin box rotated to match the roof's slope angle, computing the slope direction and midpoint to position it correctly against the cab shape.

Solving for the tilt angle gives roughly -41°, with a slight outward offset for the windshield, tinted dark cyan with a subtle glowing HUD strip. Now I'm positioning the side window boxes along the cab, matching their depth and height to the cab's side profile at the relevant z-range.

Then I'm planning out the full armor kit: angular hood and skirt plates, bull bar, roof turret with sensor mast and antenna, light bars, glowing headlight/taillight strips, exhaust stacks, fuel tanks, a cargo bed with a container and missile pods, rear ramp, rooftop RCWS turret, chevron-striped side panels, neon underglow, and decal boxes, all tied together with a dark gunmetal camo palette.

Now I'm designing the cargo module itself: a ribbed armored container sitting on the truck bed, built by extruding an angled octagonal cross-section along the vehicle's length to get the sloped, ribbed-plate look on the sides and top.

I'm closing the small gap between cab and module with a dark fifth-wheel connector block, and setting the chassis width and ground clearance beneath it.

Now I'm designing the roof turret on the module with a base cylinder, angular turret box, twin barrels, and a glowing red sensor eye, plus missile pods mounted on the module's rear top corners with tilted tube openings.

Still working out the pod geometry...

Working through the Euler angle combination, I verify that rotating the cylinder axis by 90+θ about X gives a direction matching the pod's forward tilt, confirming the math with cos65°≈0.42. I'm now generalizing this into a reusable helper for tilted positioning and cylinder orientation along arbitrary axes.

For the wheel assembly, I'm planning each tire as a 12-sided cylinder with rim, glow ring, hub bolts, and tread blocks arranged radially around the axle, computing each tread block's position using sine/cosine offsets from the wheel center.

Still defining hub stacking...

Then I'm positioning the wheels along Z for front and rear axles, checking clearance against chassis width, and adding fender arch covers over each wheel.

I'm checking for interpenetration between the fender module and wheel tops, so I'm adjusting the module's bottom height and width to keep clearance while still fitting within the chassis profile.

Now I'm sketching the chassis as a wide box beneath the cab, sized to clear the wheel inner edges and set at a height that keeps ground clearance reasonable, with fenders over the wheels approximated using simple box shapes.

I'm checking tire proportions so the tread bottom sits near ground zero without dipping noticeably, then adding cab front details—a dark grille with glowing magenta slats, slim angular headlights, and a slanted hood profile with a small nose section between the fender and windshield base.

Refining hood/front-face profile points...

Adding more side details...

Working out the viewer's orientation relative to each side so decal text reads naturally front-to-back, I decide the aim-based roll logic will handle it automatically without extra fuss. For the roof, I'm planning a glowing light bar, thin antenna masts, and a radar dish.

Now I'm sizing the exhaust stacks that sit in the gap between the cab and module, adding chrome finishes, ring clamps, and heat shields, and positioning fuel or battery tanks along the chassis sides between the wheel positions.

I'm checking the tank cylinder dimensions to make sure they clear the rear wheel's radius, then placing a glowing energy cell with green/cyan window details and strap accents. Now I'm moving to the rear of the vehicle to add red glowing tail lights.

Now I'm working out the rear chassis dimensions, bumper placement, and mudflap positions behind the rear wheels, then adding the glowing taillight strip, door seams, and ramp block to the rear module. I'm also planning the roof details—raised vents, antenna array, and solar plates—laying out the flat top width and adding hatch rings and vent grills.

For the cab, I'm sketching side mirrors, door seams and handles, armor plates, visor ridge, roof rack, wedge-shaped headlight glow bars, and hood vents, plus a sensor dome turret positioned toward the rear. For the module's camo pattern, I'm planning to generate small randomized digital-camo tiles across both sides using a three-tone palette, mirrored symmetrically with about 60 total plates.

Working through the layering so camo tiles, armor plates, and ribs sit at slightly different depths on the module's x-axis to avoid clipping into each other, while keeping the chamfered top profile in mind for placement bounds. Starting to tally up the total part count across wheels, armor, and details to get a sense of overall model complexity.

Writing builder helper functions...

I could borrow panelled() from the clockwork kit to add riveted texture to the module and cab sides cheaply, importing it from the kit path and keeping the palette under 40 colors since paints don't count toward the flat-color limit. For the extrude calls, I'll pass position, direction, thickness, bevel, and color, with the cab defaulting to standard orientation.

Working out extrude geometry for cab, module, and plow...

Still working out hood geometry...

Now I'm double-checking the windshield box rotation at θ=-41°, confirming its local axes tilt forward-up correctly, then computing the final centered position with a small outward offset so it clears the cab width.

Adding pillars, visor, and light bar...

Now I'm adding sensor details: a cyan/magenta light bar, a LIDAR cylinder with a glowing ring, a thin antenna rod with a red tip, and a radar dish built from a rotated hemisphere so it faces forward-up.

Then I'm designing the top module details: slatted vent boxes, top rails, and a remote weapon turret with a tapered wedge-shaped shell and twin gun barrels extending forward.

Positioning missile pod geometry...

Now I'm working out side cab details: a door panel plate with seams, placed on the cab side within the door region, plus a handle and seam lines, keeping the olive coloring consistent.

Next I'm adding a step below the door positioned to clear the wheels, then moving to the rear of the vehicle with glowing red tail light strips along the rear edges, rear ramp seam detailing, and a lower rear bumper box.

Still placing wheel fenders...

Now I'm adding axle cylinders at each wheel center with a dark material, plus a differential sphere and cross members underneath. I'll also add a driveshaft cylinder running along the chassis and underglow strips for detail, though I'll skip the cab-chassis skirt boxes to keep things simpler.

For branding, I'm designing an SVG decal with "NX-2077" text in bold magenta monospace font to place on the module sides, adjusting its vertical placement and height so it fits within the chamfered panel area without overshooting the top edge, settling on a plate region around y 1.4-2.1 with the decal sitting just above at y 2.28.

I'm also sketching additional emblem options—a hexagon outline with a triangle accent—for the cab doors, aligning plate thickness and decal offsets so the artwork sits flush on the outer face, and noting that the text planes should use transparent-background rasters so glow effects apply cleanly to the texture. I still need to work out the orientation axes for mirrored decals on left versus right sides and figure out the camo pattern approach.

Writing camo patch generation code...

For paint, I'm applying a panelled material with rivet detailing to both the module and cab extrusions, using slightly different tones and rivet sizes for each, since the camo and plates will mostly cover the sides anyway. I'm also considering where a lathe-generated shape might fit, possibly for an exhaust tip or similar detail.

I'm using a lathe profile to build a lidar dome, plus adding amber fog lights to the plow, a winch cylinder with cable mounted on the plow top, and small side toolboxes tucked between the rear wheels on the chassis.

Checking wheel clearances though, the gap between front and rear wheels is too tight for a toolbox, so I'm abandoning that placement and instead considering a fuel tank positioned between the wheels, sized and centered to fit beneath the module and cab without collision.

Now I'm planning the tank's end caps and strap details using thin dark cylinders rotated to wrap around it, plus a small glowing cyan energy cell strip along its outer face. Writing cylinder helper function...

Still writing wheel geometry...

Finishing up the wheel construction, keeping the output reasonably sized and double-checking syntax carefully.
